disease_label_per_paper: Catheter-related bloodstream infection caused by Luteibacter jiangsuensis in a patient with Crohn's disease and long-term central venous port
presentation_summary: 59-year-old Japanese woman with Crohn's disease on 6-mercaptopurine and infliximab had a subcutaneous central venous access port for home total parenteral nutrition.
Five days before admission she developed fever above 40 C.
Physical examination showed swelling and redness around the central venous port insertion site.

Admission CT showed a 10-mm hypodense lesion adjacent to the catheter tip in the superior vena cava; admission labs showed CRP 60.1 mg/L, procalcitonin 0.43 ng/mL, WBC 4.0 x10^9/L, and normal creatinine.

microbiology.source_text_value: gram-negative rod bacteria were detected from both sets of aerobic blood culture at 31 and 36 h
the same bacterium was also detected from the catheter-tip culture
MALDI-TOF failed; later identified as L. jiangsuensis by 16S rRNA gene sequencing
susceptibility results revealed carbapenem resistance; levofloxacin susceptible

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: same bacterium was detected from catheter-tip culture and blood cultures
patient's fever drastically improved after initial treatment
clinical examination indicated catheter-related bloodstream infection

actual_treatment.source_text_value: treatment was initiated with meropenem 1 g thrice daily
CV port/catheter was removed and catheter tip was submitted for culture
meropenem was switched to intravenous levofloxacin 500 mg/day

outcome.source_text_value: After 14 days of treatment with levofloxacin, CV port/catheter was placed, and the patient was discharged on day 18

quality_warnings: Blood-culture species, 16S identification, catheter-tip culture, susceptibility, fever response, and final CRBSI attribution are confirmatory/non-ranking.
Presentation ranking uses central-line presence, home TPN, immunosuppression, port-site inflammation, fever, CT catheter-tip lesion, and routine labs.
